intent: Run the full end-to-end suite where it can block, because CI runs smoke-only and 38 of 42 Playwright tests never execute on a pull request. Warrant WG-DEL-002 (B). Source row WO-0012. Outside the consolidation programme's phase chain and surfaced to the operator; the programme's release gate runs the full matrix locally regardless. Acceptance: (1) a main-blocking job runs the full suite with PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE unset; (2) real-hermes-integration also runs on pull_request targeting main, which is the open choice T-0002 handed to the operator when it recorded why a push-only job hid a red gate; (3) the install journey wired in, now that T-0004's committable half has landed; (4) missions-runtime.spec.ts converted to a journey, as its own header asks. Done when the suite that exists is the suite that runs. Tier proposal R2, anticipated factor ci-stateful-infra from derived signal ci-config, evidence .github/workflows/ci.yml gains a job and changes a trigger. Closed 2026-08-23. The suite is bigger than this row said: 97 Playwright tests over 13 spec files today, not 42, and PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE=1 runs 5 of them, so 92 ran on no branch. Run locally first, cold, before any wiring: 87 passed, 3 failed, 8 skipped. All three failures were defects in the tests rather than app behaviour that had gone away, and each is fixed with its assertion intact. (a) agents.spec 'profile sync controls': /Push all/i matched two buttons, ProfileSyncBar's 'Push all' and ProfilesDriftBanner's 'Push all to Hermes', so the test passed or failed on whether that run's data happened to have drifted; both are now named exactly. (b) features.spec 'optional skill detail': the test built /operations/skills/<category>/<name>, but name is already the category-qualified catalog key, so the URL carried an encoded slash and the route's path guard refused it (resolveSkillDirUnderRoot, 'Invalid skill path'). The guard is right and the URL the test built was wrong. (c) features.spec 'loads memory page': /Memory/i now matches both the h1 'Hindsight Memory' and the memory-provider tile's h2, so it is qualified to level 1. A fourth problem surfaced only when the specs ran in isolation and would have been the gate's first flake: all five agents tests fail from a cold server under a full worker pool, because the page shows 'Loading profiles...' until a post-hydration fetch resolves and Playwright's default patience is 5s. The endpoint answers in about 0.4s when timed directly, so this is first-paint contention rather than a slow route; the five now wait on the 30s ceiling the rest of the suite already uses, and retries stay at zero. missions-runtime.spec.ts is a journey now instead of three render assertions: a saved mission put on a timer, the preset actually taking the cadence field, the schedule created, paused, surviving a reload, then removed, plus Scripts reached through the sidebar rather than asserted to exist. Every affordance the old file covered is still touched on the way through. Three consecutive full runs after the fixes: 89 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed, 33 to 47 seconds (7 of the skips are the opt-in screenshot captures behind CAPTURE_SCREENSHOTS, the 8th is a story-detail test that skips on an empty library). WIRED: e2e-full runs npm run test:e2e with PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE unset on pull_request into main plus workflow_dispatch, 30 minute timeout, differing from e2e-smoke by exactly that one environment variable so the two cannot drift into different suites; real-hermes-integration's if gained the same pull-request-into-main clause with push and dispatch untouched; acceptance-gate aggregates e2e-full, install-harness and real-hermes-integration into a single check, which is how the install journey enters the blocking set and how its membership becomes a diff. NOT DONE, and not doable from inside the repository: branch protection on main requires zero checks, so acceptance-gate reports and blocks nothing until the operator makes it required. That is the same wall T-0004 hit and it is now one click for the whole set rather than one per job. TWO FINDINGS RAISED, NOT FIXED, both outside these claims: the scheduled-mission delete control is an unlabelled icon button with no accessible name, so the journey has to reach it positionally; and every run recorded here is on Windows, so the Linux runner's first green e2e-full is still unread and the same caution T-0004 applied to install-harness applies to this job. PROVEN ON CI 2026-08-23, after the row first closed: e2e-full's first real Linux run failed 1 of 88, which is exactly the caution the review attached (every local run had been on Windows). The cause was not the test. Playwright starts webServer BEFORE globalSetup, and global-setup wiped the data dir while the server held the database it had just seeded at boot; the next query recreated an EMPTY database, because migrations rerun through getDb() but the catalogue seed only runs at boot, which had passed. It never reproduced locally for two independent reasons: on Windows the wipe fails with EPERM because SQLite holds the handles, and .env.local's PS_DATA_DIR resolves ahead of the CH_DATA_DIR the config sets, so local runs were silently testing the developer's own database rather than tmp/e2e-data. Fixed in 703d83d7 by wiping BEFORE boot and forcing PS_DATA_DIR on the spawned server; global-setup now asserts the catalogue is visible instead of deleting it. e2e-full and acceptance-gate are both green on PR #157. No assertion was relaxed and nothing was skipped.
